title: That view condemned by Pius V and Gregory XIII (Baius' articles 21 and 26)
source_text: V. Verum haec sententia fuit a Pontificibus Romanis videlicet, Pio V. & Gregorio XIII. superiori saeculo damnata. Nam inter multos articulos in singulari Bulla horum Pontificum damnatos, iste est vigesimus primus. Humanae naturae sublimatio, & exaltatio in consortium divinae debita fuit integritati primae conditionis, ac proinde naturalis dicenda est, non supernaturalis. Sextus vero & vigesimus his verbis conceptus est, Integritas primae conditionis non fuit indebita humanae naturae exaltatio, sed ejus naturalis conditio. Ut refert Bellarminus de gratia primi hominis, lib. unico, cap. 1.
pass_a_gloss: But this opinion was condemned by the Roman Pontiffs, namely, Pius V. and Gregory XIII. in the last century. For among the many articles condemned in a singular Bull of these Pontiffs, this is the twenty-first. The sublimation and exaltation of human nature into the fellowship of the divine was owed to the integrity of the first condition, and therefore must be called natural, not supernatural. But the twenty-sixth is conceived in these words, The integrity of the first condition was not an unowed exaltation of human nature, but its natural condition. As Bellarmine reports on the grace of the first man, sole book, chap. 1.
pass_b_english: Popes Pius V and Gregory XIII condemned this view in the last century. In their bull, which condemned many articles together, it appears as article 21: "Human nature's being lifted up and raised into partnership with the divine nature was owed to the integrity of man's first condition, and is therefore to be called natural, not supernatural."

Article 26 runs: "The integrity of man's first condition was not an exaltation of human nature beyond its due, but its natural condition." Bellarmine records this in chapter 1 of his single book On the Grace of the First Man.

choices.english: into partnership with the divine nature
choices.why: Consortium divinae (naturae) recalls 2 Peter 1:4, 'partakers of the divine nature'.
